texts.exact_text: Thung Zăn (or Union of men) appears here (as we find it) in the (remote districts of the) country, indicating progress and success. It will be advantageous to cross the great stream. It will be advantageous to maintain the firm correctness of the superior man.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 13; scan-backed transcription p. 86, hexagram statement
texts.notes: Legge's title restored from the source statement.

texts.exact_text: The first NINE, undivided, (shows the representative of) the union of men just issuing from his gate. There will be no error.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 13; scan-backed transcription p. 86, line 1

texts.exact_text: The second SIX, divided, (shows the representative of) the union of men in relation with his kindred. There will be occasion for regret.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 13; scan-backed transcription p. 86, line 2

texts.exact_text: The third NINE, undivided, (shows its subject) with his arms hidden in the thick grass, and at the top of a high mound. (But) for three years he makes no demonstration.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 13; scan-backed transcription p. 86, line 3

texts.exact_text: The fourth NINE, undivided, (shows its subject) mounted on the city wall; but he does not proceed to make the attack (he contemplates). There will be good fortune.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 13; scan-backed transcription p. 86, line 4

texts.exact_text: In the fifth NINE, undivided, (the representative of) the union of men first wails and cries out, and then laughs. His great host conquers, and he (and the subject of the second line) meet together.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 13; scan-backed transcription p. 86, line 5

texts.exact_text: The topmost NINE, undivided, (shows the representative of) the union of men in the suburbs. There will be no occasion for repentance.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 13; scan-backed transcription p. 86, line 6

texts.exact_text:
Thung Zăn describes a condition of nature and of the state opposite to that of Phî. There was distress and obstruction; here is union. But the union must be based entirely on public considerations, without taint of selfishness.

The strong line in the fifth, its correct, place, occupies the most important position, and has for its correlate the weak second line, also in its correct place. The one divided line is naturally sought after by all the strong lines. The upper trigram ☰ is that of heaven, which is above; the lower ☲ is that of fire, whose tendency is to mount upwards. All these things are in harmony with the idea of union. But the union must be free from all selfish motives, and this is indicated by its being in the remote districts of the country, where people are unsophisticated, and free from the depraving effects incident to large societies. A union from such motives will cope with the greatest difficulties; and yet a word of caution is added.

Line 1 emblems the first attempts at union. It is strong, but in the lowest place; and it has no proper correlate above. There is, however, no intermixture of selfishness in it.

Lines 2 and 5 are proper correlates, which fact suggests in this hexagram the idea of their union being limited and partial, and such as may afford ground for blame.

Line 3 is strong, and in an odd place; but it has not a proper correlate in 6. This makes its subject more anxious to unite with 2; but 2 is devoted to its proper correlate in 5, of whose strength 3 is afraid, and takes the measures described. His abstaining so long, however, from any active attempt, will save him from misfortune.

Line 4 is strong, but in an even place, which weakens its subject, He also would fain make an attempt on 2; but he is afraid, and does not carry his purpose into effect.

Line 5 is strong, in an odd, and the central place; and would fain unite with 2, which indeed is the proper correlate of its subject. But 3 and 4 are powerful foes that oppose the union, Their opposition makes him weep; but he collects his forces, defeats them, and effects his purpose.

The union reaches to all within the suburbs (郊), and is riot yet universal; but still there is no cause for repentance. 同人 ䷌
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Hexagram 13; scan-backed transcription p. 86, notes

texts.exact_text: 同人于野，亨。 利涉大川，利君子貞。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 易經卦辭

texts.exact_text: 同人，柔得位得中，而應乎乾，曰同人。同人曰，同人于野，亨。利涉大川，乾行也。文明以健，中正而應，君子正也。唯君子為能通天下之志。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 彖

texts.exact_text: 天與火，同人；君子以類族辨物。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 大象

texts.exact_text: 初九：同人于門，無咎。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 爻 1

texts.exact_text: 出門同人，又誰咎也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 小象 1

texts.exact_text: 六二：同人于宗，吝。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 爻 2

texts.exact_text: 同人于宗，吝道也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 小象 2

texts.exact_text: 九三：伏戎于莽，升其高陵，三歲不興。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 爻 3

texts.exact_text: 伏戎于莽，敵剛也。三歲不興，安行也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 小象 3

texts.exact_text: 九四：乘其墉，弗克，攻吉。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 爻 4

texts.exact_text: 乘其墉，義弗克也，其吉，則困而反則也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 小象 4

texts.exact_text: 九五：同人，先號啕而后笑。大師克相遇。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 爻 5

texts.exact_text: 同人之先，以中直也。大師相遇，言相克也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 小象 5

texts.exact_text: 上九：同人于郊，無悔。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 爻 6

texts.exact_text: 同人于郊，志未得也。
texts.locator: Chinese Wikisource 周易/同人; cross-checked against CTP Book of Changes, hexagram 13, 小象 6

texts.exact_text:
In Thung Zăn the weak (line) has the place (of influence), the central place (☲), and responds to (the corresponding line in) ☰ Qián (above); hence comes its name of Thung Zăn (or 'Union of men').

Thung Zăn says:

The language, 'Thung Zăn appears here (as we find it) in (the remote districts of) the country, indicating progress and success, and that it will be advantageous to cross the great stream,' is moulded by its containing the strength (symbolled) in ☰ Qián. (Then) we have (the trigram indicating) elegance and intelligence, supported by (that indicating) strength; with the line in the central, and its correct, position, and responding (to the corresponding line above): -- (all representing) the correct course of the superior man. It is only the superior man who can comprehend and affect the minds of all under the sky.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix I, Hexagram 13, p. 226

texts.exact_text: (The trigrams ☰ ☲ for) heaven and fire form Thung Zăn. The superior man, in accordance with this), distinguishes things according to their kinds and classes.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 13, p. 285

texts.exact_text: '(The representative of) the union of men is just issuing from his gate:' -- who will blame him?
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 13, line 1, p. 285

texts.exact_text: '(The representative of) the union of men appears in relation with his kindred:' -- that is the path to regret.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 13, line 2, p. 285

texts.exact_text: 'He hides his arms in the thick grass:' -- because of the strength of his opponent. 'For three years he makes no demonstration:' -- how can he do anything?
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 13, line 3, p. 285

texts.exact_text: 'He is mounted on his city-wall;' but yielding to the right, 'he does not proceed to make the attack (he contemplated).' (Where it is said),'There will be good fortune,' (that shows how) he feels the strait he is in, and returns to the rule of law.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 13, line 4, p. 285

texts.exact_text: The first action of (the representative of) the union of men (here described) arises from his central position and straightforward character. 'The meeting secured by his great host' intimates that the opponents of it have been overcome.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 13, line 5, p. 285

texts.exact_text: '(The representative of) the union of men appears in the suburbs:' -- his object has not yet been attained.
texts.locator: SBE XVI, Appendix II, Hexagram 13, line 6, p. 285
